questions.question: In the slack form of an LP, a basic solution is found by setting some variables to zero and solving the equations for the rest. Why can a basic solution be infeasible?
options: Setting variables to zero breaks the equations
The zero variables violate their sign condition
Basic solutions never satisfy the objective
The solved-for variables can come out negative

questions.question: An LP has constraints $x_1+x_2\le4$, $x_1+3x_2\le6$, written as $x_1+x_2+s_1=4$, $x_1+3x_2+s_2=6$ with $x_1,x_2,s_1,s_2\ge0$. Is the interior point $(x_1,x_2)=(1,1)$ a basic solution?
options: Yes: it satisfies both equations with nonnegative values
No: all four values are nonzero, but two must be zero
Yes: every feasible point is a basic solution of the system
No: a basic solution must have $x_1=x_2=0$

questions.question: A system has equations $x_1+x_2+s_1=10$, $x_1+s_2=3$ in variables $x_1,x_2,s_1,s_2$. Why does the choice $x_1=0$, $s_2=0$ give no basic solution?
options: It gives $x_2=10$ and $s_1=0$ instead
It gives a negative value for $s_1$
It sets an original variable to zero
The second equation turns into $0=3$

questions.question: A system has $m=2$ independent equations in $n=4$ variables. A student sets only ONE variable to zero and tries to solve for the other three. What goes wrong?
options: The resulting point is always infeasible, as one value is negative
Nothing; any number of zeros gives a basic solution
The system has no solution, as there are too few zeros
Three unknowns in two equations leave infinitely many solutions

questions.question: A basic solution of an LP in slack form has $x_1,x_2\ge0$ but one slack variable negative. A student says it is feasible because the decision variables are nonnegative. What is wrong?
options: A negative slack means its constraint is violated
Nothing; slacks are helper variables without signs
Basic solutions are feasible as soon as $x\ge0$
Only the objective decides whether it is feasible

questions.question: The system $x_1+x_2+s_1=4$ and $x_1+3x_2+s_2=6$ (the constraints $x_1+x_2\le4$, $x_1+3x_2\le6$ with slacks; all variables must be $\ge0$ for feasibility) has the four feasible basic solutions $(x_1,x_2)=(0,0),(4,0),(3,1),(0,2)$. The constraint $x_1\le2.5$ is added with slack $s_3$. How many of these four points remain feasible basic solutions?
